title: No Singing In The Navy by Milo Cramer at Playwrights Horizons #nosing...
transcript: Three silly sailors have docked in a city, setting out to make the most of 24 hours in comedically musical fashion — sound familiar? In this homage to and satire of the classic American musical, three actors and a pianist both capture and critique the aching innocence and the unearned optimism engrained in American culture, all through a zany and ridiculous lens. It doesn't really follow a traditional narrative structure, nor does it need to for your attention — it's only 80 minutes long and constantly shifting. The humor is offbeat and wonderfully stupid — it won't be for everyone, but there's much to appreciate in the unexpectedly specific and idiosyncratic choices in the writing and in the performances. My personal favorite scene was between two ants and a crab. Although this show doesn't have the same perfect blend of humor and bite as Milo Cramer's more personal piece School Pictures, I thought this was still an enjoyable showcase of their distinctive voice as a writer. With that, another program for my collection.
